upcoming.headline: Remington Museum open Veterans Day, 11 AM-4 PM
upcoming.briefing: The Frederic Remington Art Museum in Ogdensburg will be open from 11 a.m. to 4 p.m. on Veterans Day, Wednesday, Nov 11, per @remingtonmuseumofart on Nov 10. The museum pitched it as a place to spend time with art for anyone with the day off. Watch for holiday attendance and any Veterans Day programming.

upcoming.headline: Last Free Fishing Day of 2026 is Wednesday
upcoming.briefing: Wednesday, Nov 11 is the last Free Fishing Day of 2026, per @lakeplacidadk on Nov 8. No freshwater fishing license is needed anywhere in New York that day, so anyone can grab a rod and fish the region's waters for free. Lake Placid's picks around town include the West Branch Ausable River, Upper and Lower Cascade Lakes, Lake Placid itself, and the South and North Forks of the Boquet River. The day falls on Veterans Day, so it is a free outing that lines up with a day off for many.

upcoming.headline: Chamber names its 2026 award winners
upcoming.briefing: The Potsdam Chamber has named its 2026 award winners ahead of its annual dinner, per @potsdamchamber in the Nov 2 sweep. The 2026 Annual Dinner and Awards take place Thursday, November 12, at The Stables at Windy Point, honoring Third Wheel Pottery Studio as Business of the Year, NoCo Superior Exterior LLC for Pride in Potsdam, and Stone and Steel Gym for Commitment to the Community. The Chamber notes that Friday's registration deadline has passed but asks anyone still hoping to attend to send a direct message as soon as possible. Watch for the dinner turnout and the acceptance remarks, since the three honorees span retail, trades, and fitness in town.
upcoming.location: The Stables at Windy Point, Potsdam

upcoming.headline: '2AM' opens Friday at SLC Arts
upcoming.briefing: SLC Arts has a new original play on stage this weekend, per @slcartsny on Nov 8. '2AM,' an original play by Nick Attanasio that ran off-Broadway, comes to Potsdam with local actors, including Emily Reed-Fecketter as Shelly, for performances Friday, Nov 13 and Saturday, Nov 14 at 7 PM, doors at 6:30. The diner-set comedy follows Matthew, Anthony, and Brian through their relationship woes at 2 a.m. Tickets are $24, with a pay-it-forward option to help cover actor pay. The play is part of a busy SLC Arts week that also includes a jazz group and digital collage classes.

upcoming.headline: Lucky Night Market set for November 13 in Potsdam
upcoming.briefing: The Potsdam Chamber of Commerce is lining up a holiday head start in downtown Potsdam, per @potsdamchamber on Nov 3. The Lucky Night Market runs Friday, November 13, from 5 to 8 p.m. at Market Square Mall, 22 Depot Street, with local vendors selling art, crochet, jewelry, candy and more. The pitch is simple: a little local shopping, a few sweet treats, and support for small businesses before the holiday rush. Watch for a vendor list and any parking or weather notes as November 13 gets closer.

upcoming.headline: Original play '2AM' set for Nov 13-14
upcoming.briefing: SLC Arts is putting a homegrown play on stage next month, per @slcartsny on Oct 24. The original play 2AM was written by Nick Attanasio and features a cast of local actors. Performances are Nov 13 and 14, with doors at 6:30 PM and curtain at 7 PM. Tickets are $24, with pay-it-forward options for buyers who want to cover a seat for someone else. Watch: ticket sales and whether the local cast draws a Potsdam crowd beyond the usual arts audience.

upcoming.headline: Fall Open House set for Saturday, Nov 14
upcoming.briefing: Clarkson University holds its next Fall Open House on Saturday, Nov 14, per @clarksonuniv on Nov 10. Prospective students can tour campus, see hands-on learning, and get a feel for life as a Golden Knight. Registration is open now. Watch for turnout and any follow-up admissions deadlines tied to the visit.

upcoming.headline: Flannel Fest takes over downtown Canton Saturday
upcoming.briefing: Flannel Fest returns to downtown Canton on Saturday, November 14, per the Facebook event listing found November 9. The celebration of local businesses runs during each shop's own business hours, with stores along Main Street featuring flannel-themed specials as holiday shopping gets underway. Organizers are asking shoppers to wear flannel and spend locally, calling each dollar spent downtown an investment in the businesses that support local teams, events, and organizations. The event is centered at 60 Main Street in Canton, and 70 people had marked themselves interested as of this morning.

upcoming.headline: US Veterans MC St. Lawrence Chapter marks 13 years in Ogdensburg
upcoming.briefing: The US Veterans MC St. Lawrence Chapter holds its 13th anniversary party on Nov 14 at 1 PM at the Ogdensburg VFW on Champlain Street, per the Facebook event. The $20 donation covers food, music, and raffles. Veterans motorcycle clubs are a durable part of the North Country civic fabric, and the VFW post remains their anchor venue. Interest is modest but the chapter's annual parties reliably draw from across the county.

upcoming.headline: Vision-board workshop lands in Norwood Nov 14
upcoming.briefing: A vision-board workshop called The Vision Within runs Nov 14 from 1 to 4 PM at the Melting Pot Community Center in Norwood, per the Facebook event. It is led by a licensed clinical social worker, a spiritual wellness coach, and a painting-party host, blending therapeutic and creative framing. Norwood rarely shows up in the event feed, so this is a useful data point for the town's small wellness scene. Registration runs through the organizers' booking page.

upcoming.headline: NNY Women Who Lead holds first women's self-defense class Nov 15
upcoming.briefing: NNY Women Who Lead holds its first-ever Women's Self-Defense Class on Sunday, November 15, at 1 PM at American Top Team Watertown Martial Arts & Fitness, per the group's Facebook event on Nov 5. Coach Rachel Huntsman of American Top Team leads the jiu-jitsu-based session, designed for women of all ages and abilities. The class aims to build confidence and teach practical self-defense skills in a group setting. The listing shows 13 people going and 149 interested, a strong early response for a first-time offering. The venue is at 223 JB Wise Place in Watertown.
upcoming.location: American Top Team Watertown, 223 JB Wise Pl, Watertown, NY

upcoming.headline: Fall candle workshop Nov 15 in Hannawa Falls
upcoming.briefing: A fall candle-making workshop called Fall Into Fragrance runs November 15 from 1 to 3 PM at StoneWear Studio in Hannawa Falls, per the Facebook event listing found November 2. Michele from Scented Smiles and Ashley Taillon, a spiritual wellness coach, lead the session, which pairs hands-on candle making with fall fragrances, decorations, and crystals. The afternoon also includes a guided meditation for intention setting and a guided EFT tapping session focused on release and reset. Tickets are $33 per person, spots are limited, and attendees take home the candle they make.

upcoming.handle: Spruce Mill Brook Christmas Tree Farm
upcoming.headline: Wreath workshops open in Waddington Nov 16
upcoming.briefing: Spruce Mill Brook Christmas Tree Farm has opened booking for its wreath workshops in Waddington, per the farm's Facebook event listing found Oct 29. The first listed workshop runs Monday, November 16 at 6:00 PM, offering a festive wreath-making session for friends and family. Spots are capped at 8 per workshop, so the small-group format is part of the draw. Booking runs through the link on the event listing. Holiday workshops in a small St. Lawrence County village tend to fill on word of mouth, so early booking matters here.
upcoming.location: Spruce Mill Brook Christmas Tree Farm, Waddington, NY
upcoming.who: Spruce Mill Brook Christmas Tree Farm

upcoming.headline: Potsdam Chamber welcomes Roxy Tattoo with ribbon cutting Nov 17
upcoming.briefing: The Potsdam Chamber of Commerce hosts a meet-the-artist and ribbon cutting for Roxy Tattoo on Tuesday, November 17, from noon to 1 PM at 20 Main Street in downtown Potsdam, per the Chamber's Facebook event on Nov 5. The event welcomes the tattoo studio and its owner Nya as a new downtown business. The Chamber frames it as a celebration of creativity and entrepreneurship in the village core. The midday slot is a short drop-in format, aimed at downtown foot traffic and fellow business owners. It is the latest in the Chamber's run of downtown ribbon cuttings for new storefronts.
upcoming.location: Roxy Tattoo, 20 Main St, Potsdam, NY

upcoming.headline: Youth Nordic ski rentals open; apply by Nov 20
upcoming.briefing: The Potsdam Public Library and SUNY Potsdam's Wilderness Education Program opened sign-ups for the Youth Nordic Ski Program, per @potsdampubliclibrary on Nov 10. The program offers season-long cross-country ski rentals for children ages 3 to 17, running November 2026 through April 2027, for $100 per child, with scholarships for families receiving SNAP benefits. Applications are due Friday, Nov 20, and equipment is limited. Watch whether demand outruns the available gear.

upcoming.headline: SLC Arts Holiday Mixer offers $5 custom poems
upcoming.briefing: SLC Arts will feature poet Ryan Murphy at its Holiday Mixer on November 20, writing custom poems on the spot for $5 each, per @slcartsny on Oct 30. The mixer is the arts council's fourth annual winter gathering, and the post frames the poems as a ready-made unique gift. Pre-registration is open through the SLC Arts online shop. For Potsdam, this is the first firm date on the holiday arts calendar, and it lands a week before the downtown holiday season kicks into full gear. Watch for the full mixer lineup as November 20 approaches.

upcoming.headline: Composting drop-in at the Children's Museum Nov 21
upcoming.briefing: The North Country Children's Museum will host a composting and food-waste drop-in on Saturday, November 21, from 10 AM to 1 PM, per @nccmuseum on Oct 29. Visitors can make garlands from dehydrated fruit, print greeting cards with vegetable stamps, and explore the science of composting, all included with museum admission. The event is staged with Clarkson Sustainability and the Village of Potsdam, a sign of how the museum keeps pairing kid-friendly making with real local partners. Mark it as a family morning option well ahead of the holiday stretch.

upcoming.headline: Flying Ivories dueling pianos return to Pike's Place Nov 21
upcoming.briefing: The Flying Ivories Dueling Pianos return to Pike's Place in Brasher Falls for a third consecutive year on Saturday, November 21, per the Pike's Place Facebook event listing found Oct 29. Doors open at 6:00 PM and the show starts at 7:30 PM, built around music, laughter, sing-alongs, and song requests. General admission is $25 plus Eventbrite fees, with table reservations available for an additional $20. Gideon's Galley will be on site selling food. With 204 people marked interested, this is shaping up as one of the busier November nights in the Brasher Falls area.
upcoming.location: Pike's Place, 138 County Route 50, Brasher Falls, NY

upcoming.headline: Kids play 'Going Nuts' hits the museum stage Nov 22
upcoming.briefing: The North Country Children's Museum in Potsdam has a new kids' stage production on the calendar, per @nccmuseum on Nov 8. 'Going Nuts: A Play for Kids and Families' runs Sunday, Nov 22 at 2 PM on the museum stage, and admission is included in the price of admission or membership. The story follows Nelson the gray squirrel and his Grandpa Quercus hunting for buried acorns, with the audience helping the squirrels find the stash. It is a family daytime event two weeks out, worth a note for anyone planning a Potsdam weekend with kids.

upcoming.headline: Grown-Up Book Fair returns to The Strand in Watertown Nov 22
upcoming.briefing: The Grown-Up Book Fair is back at The Strand Theater in Watertown on Sunday, November 22, starting at 10 AM, per the Strand Theater Facebook event on Nov 5. The fair is presented by HarmoNNY Performing Arts Community, Spoken Word of NNY, The NEST, and Neighbors of Watertown. The listing shows 107 people going and nearly 1,800 interested, making it one of the bigger Watertown draws on the November calendar. The Strand at 136 Franklin Street hosts the fair again after running it before. The event gives adult readers a book-fair format usually aimed at kids, with local arts groups behind it.
upcoming.location: The Strand Theater, 136 Franklin St, Watertown, NY

upcoming.headline: Cards, Crystals, and Cocktails afternoon in Parishville Nov 22
upcoming.briefing: An afternoon of tarot readings, crystals, and permanent jewelry is set for Sunday, November 22 from 1 to 4 PM at AMVETS Post #265 in Parishville, per the Facebook event listing found Nov 4. Tarot readings come from Ashley Taillon, crystals and minerals from StoneWear Creations, and permanent jewelry from Forever Jewelry Studio by Ashlyn. The listing frames it as a social afternoon for friends, with drinks and browsing alongside the readings and shopping. Interest is already solid, with 96 people marked interested against 10 going, so this reads as a small but real draw for the Parishville area on a late-November Sunday.

upcoming.headline: Family matinee: Monty Python and the Holy Grail at the library Nov 22
upcoming.briefing: The Potsdam Public Library will screen the 1975 cult comedy Monty Python and the Holy Grail as a family-friendly matinee on Sunday, November 22 at 2 PM, per the Facebook event listing found Nov 4. The film loosely follows the legend of King Arthur and his Knights of the Round Table, with Graham Chapman, John Cleese, Eric Idle, Terry Jones, Michael Palin, and Terry Gilliam. The screening is at the library at 2 Park Street in Potsdam. As a free, all-ages library program on a Sunday afternoon, it fits the library's steady run of community programming heading into the holiday season.
upcoming.location: Potsdam Public Library, 2 Park St, Potsdam, NY

upcoming.headline: Winter Wonderland at Gran View opens November 27
upcoming.briefing: Winter Wonderland at Gran View in Ogdensburg opens on November 27, now 29 days out, per @granviewontheriver on Oct 30. The post shows setup already taking shape behind the scenes and promises more details as opening approaches. The late-November start plants it squarely in the post-Thanksgiving holiday season, and Gran View is positioning it as a returning seasonal draw on the St. Lawrence River. For Ogdensburg, it is an early signal that the holiday events calendar is filling in. Watch for ticket, hours and attraction details in the coming weeks.

upcoming.headline: Chamber rounds up Small Business Saturday deals
upcoming.briefing: The North Country Chamber of Commerce is building its Small Business Saturday roundup, per @ncountrychamber on Nov 8. The Chamber is collecting local holiday specials, exclusive discounts, gift-card deals, and giveaways into one place so shoppers can find them and keep holiday spending local. Participation is free, and businesses can submit their offer at the link in the Chamber's bio. Small Business Saturday falls Nov 28 this year, three weeks out, so the roundup will fill in over the coming days.

upcoming.headline: Karaoke night with Given Lyrics at Stadium Sports Bar Dec 4
upcoming.briefing: Karaoke lovers in the Canton and Potsdam area have a December date to circle, per the Stadium Sports Bar Facebook event listing. Given Lyrics hosts karaoke night at The Stadium Sports Bar in Canton on Friday, Dec 4, from 7 to 11 PM, with a catalog of more than 60,000 songs and a crowd the event pitches as loyal and supportive. The bar offers drinks, sports on the TVs, and indoor golf on its Upper Deck, with Sergi's next door for food. Cards are accepted with a $10 minimum and an ATM is on site. The event is framed as a room that listens and cheers, whether singers are brand new or seasoned regulars.
upcoming.location: The Stadium Sports Bar, Canton, NY

upcoming.headline: Exceptional Art Club returns to Ogdensburg Dec 5
upcoming.briefing: The St. Lawrence County Exceptional Art Club holds its next session Saturday, December 5, from 1:30 to 3:30 p.m. at St. John's Episcopal Church in Ogdensburg, per the Facebook event listing found November 9. The club is a welcoming, inclusive art experience designed for children with higher support needs, ages 2 through high school, in a sensory-aware environment where kids explore creativity at their own pace. Each session offers adaptive, process-focused art activities meant to build self-expression, confidence, and joy, with no prior art experience needed, and families and caregivers are welcome to support participation. Registration is through the ticket link on the event page or at encompassrec.com.
upcoming.location: St. John's Episcopal Church, 500 Caroline St, Ogdensburg

upcoming.headline: Light the Night Parade set for December 5 downtown
upcoming.briefing: Downtown Potsdam lights up for the Light the Night Parade on Saturday, December 5 at 6 p.m., per @potsdamchamber on Nov 5. The chamber is recruiting decorated vehicles, floats and lighted walking groups, with businesses, organizations, families and friends all welcome. Sign-ups close November 20 at potsdamchamber.com. The parade is the village’s main holiday kickoff, and the month-long runway gives groups time to build entries. Watch for the route and lineup once registration closes.

upcoming.headline: Art of Manifesting workshop in Norwood Dec 5
upcoming.briefing: Spirit & Soul Wellness brings The Art of Manifesting to The Melting Pot Community Center in Norwood on Saturday, December 5, per the Spirit & Soul Wellness Facebook event listing found Oct 29. The 10 AM to noon workshop, led by Ashley Taillon, covers manifestation education, the law of attraction, an EFT tapping session, grounding and guided meditation, intention setting, and journaling. Attendees also make a personalized manifestation kit to take home. Individual tickets are $44 and spots are limited. No experience is needed, which pitches the morning at newcomers as much as regular wellness attendees.
upcoming.location: The Melting Pot Community Center, Norwood, NY

upcoming.headline: Chemistry magic show benefits Potsdam Holiday Fund Dec 5
upcoming.briefing: Per the Facebook event "Dr. Jim's Chemistry Magic Show to Benefit the PHF" on Oct 22: Clarkson University professor Jim Peploski will stage his annual "Miracles, Magic and Mayhem" chemistry demonstration show at 11 a.m. on Saturday, Dec 5 in Room 360 of Clarkson's Science Center. The show, aimed at children but pitched as fun for all ages, features 10 to 15 demonstrations including liquid-nitrogen ice cream samples. It benefits the Potsdam Holiday Fund, which provides new toys, clothing, boots and food to families and senior citizens in need across Potsdam, Madrid, Hopkinton, Nicholville, Brasher Falls, Chase Mills, Fort Jackson, West Stockholm and Winthrop. Each attendee is asked to bring one new unwrapped toy or gift; monetary contributions are also welcome. The event is sponsored by Peploski and the Clarkson Department of Chemistry and Biomolecular Science.
upcoming.location: Science Center Room 360, Clarkson University, Potsdam

upcoming.headline: Light the Night Parade returns Dec 5 with Ives Park tree lighting
upcoming.briefing: The Potsdam Chamber of Commerce and the Village of Potsdam will stage the annual Light the Night Parade on Dec 5, with lineup at 5 PM, the parade rolling at 6, and a community celebration plus tree lighting at Ives Park from 6:30 to 7:30, per the Facebook event. Glowing floats and the riverfront tree lighting make this the formal kickoff of the downtown holiday season. More than 1,200 people have marked themselves interested, signaling another big turnout. Bundle-up weather is a given; Ives Park is the visual anchor of the night.

upcoming.headline: Santa breakfast and dinner set at Gran View
upcoming.briefing: Santa is coming to Winter Wonderland at Gran View on the River in Ogdensburg, per @granviewontheriver on Nov 10. Breakfast with Santa runs Sunday, Dec 6, from 9 a.m. to noon, with a buffet and a visit with Santa for $24 ages 12 and up and $21 for ages 3 to 11. Dinner with Santa follows Friday, Dec 18, from 5 to 8 p.m., ordering from the regular dinner menu. Reservations are required for both. Watch for sellouts as December approaches.
upcoming.location: Gran View on the River, Ogdensburg

upcoming.headline: Holiday photos with Santa at Canton clinic Dec 6
upcoming.briefing: Per the Facebook event "Photos with Santa" on Oct 22: the holiday event runs Sunday, Dec 6 from 11 a.m. to 3 p.m. at 2750 State Highway 68 in Canton, with Santa available throughout for photos with kids, families, and pets. The walkthrough also includes holiday crafts, face painting, cookies, and festive drinks. Interest stands at 63 interested and 11 going with six weeks to build. The address points to a Canton business location rather than a public venue.

upcoming.headline: Open enrollment deadlines land in December
upcoming.briefing: Open enrollment deadlines are closing in, per @mynbc5 on Nov 5. December 15 is the last day to enroll in ACA Marketplace coverage beginning January 1, and December 7 is the deadline to change Medicare coverage. Premium costs and Medicare Part D drug plans shift in 2027, so coverage could look different next year. The post points viewers to the link in bio for what is changing. Anyone on a Marketplace or Medicare plan should check their options before the deadlines pass.

upcoming.handle: David Sauther Memorial Winter Wonderland Craft Show
upcoming.headline: 12th annual Winter Wonderland craft show in Malone Dec 12
upcoming.briefing: Per the Facebook event "12th Annual David Sauther Memorial Winter Wonderland Craft & Vendor Show" on Oct 22: the show runs Saturday, Dec 12 from 6 a.m. to noon at Davis Elementary School, 183 Webster St., Malone. Organizers describe it as a huge, well-advertised show with a wide variety of participants, and crafters, artisans and direct-sale vendors are signing up now. The listing shows 150 interested and 44 going, a strong early pull for a December date. This is the furthest-east Franklin County entry on this run's radar.
upcoming.location: Davis Elementary School, 183 Webster St, Malone
upcoming.who: David Sauther Memorial Winter Wonderland Craft Show

upcoming.headline: DEC forest grants open; North Country municipalities face Dec 16 deadline
upcoming.briefing: The state Department of Environmental Conservation is offering $1.5 million statewide in the fourth round of its Community Forest Conservation Grant Program, per Ogdensburg News. North Country municipalities have until 3 PM on Dec 16, 2026, to file applications through SFS Grants Management; they must name specific parcels and willing landowners, with appraisals, a municipal resolution, and a signed landowner agreement. DEC is hosting an application webinar Oct 21 at 10 AM for municipal officials preparing bids.
